# RI and repository understanding: completed Work factorial study

The tested RI treatment did **not demonstrate incremental conceptual-quality
benefit**, and neither frozen primary benefit gate passed. All 12 first answers
received 2/2 from the separate assessor: all five criteria met and no serious
errors. Adding RI to AGENTS reduced recorded source/RI operations from 119 to
108 (9.2%), while measured supplied input increased from 854,465 to 1,143,067
UTF-8 bytes (33.8%). This supports no mandatory full-context-loading change.
It does not establish that RI is generally ineffective.

All 12 original outcomes were published individually to PR #125, including
first answers, complete reader journals and native-output caches. No response
was replaced, repaired or selectively repeated. The series is complete and
stops here as planned. The earlier interrupted study and inventory pilot remain
separate and byte-identical to their previous committed versions.

## What the comparison establishes

This is the newly authorized September 21 execution of the prepared three
tasks, not recovery of the lost earlier workers. All participants used source
`989fc1398fc221ffca4e1f7a141b2c03bfc7cfb3`, regardless of later PR publications.
The input freeze was remotely published at
`48a1c9964de47ed3545824981ebaf96e4d6723c9` before the first dispatch.

| Condition | Original root/applicable scoped AGENTS | Native RI treatment | Ordinary sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | Unavailable | Unavailable | Available |
| AGENTS | Complete text required | Unavailable | Available |
| RI | Unavailable | Supplied and queryable | Available |
| AGENTS_RI | Complete text required | Supplied and queryable | Available |

The primary question is the added value of RI **over AGENTS**. Original
instruction text was not automatically supplied to every participant. The
reader applied condition permissions to listings, search results and reads.
Ordinary README, CONTRIBUTING, doctrine, patterns and RI architecture remained
shared; therefore NONE means neither tested aid, not absence of all navigation
or all repository knowledge. Native RI retains structural AGENTS metadata,
which is different from receiving the complete original instruction text.

Both RI conditions received the accepted producer's verification result and
the complete `context-for-task` output for the exact Ukrainian task. No
translation, custom summary, ranking repair or shortened inventory was
inserted. Additional accepted native operations remained available. This tests
forced delivery of the native task-context output, not the normal optional
route, every RI feature, the full graph, Control Map or the maintainer's iPad
client. Supplied output proves exposure through the reader, not internal use.

Twelve fresh native Work sessions used `fork_turns=none`, inherited configured
model settings and no model/reasoning overrides. There were at most three
active test sessions. Each replacement slot was dispatched only after a
previous outcome's remote commit/tree was verified. Exact serving backend,
hidden platform input and platform-wide isolation remain unverified.

## Quality and conceptual distinctions

| Task | NONE | AGENTS | RI | AGENTS_RI | Observed conceptual outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1: request routing and Thinking System | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | All distinguish consequential Model Judgment from deterministic execution; enum/schema enforcement from semantic correctness; a flag from authorized, timely control |
| F2: proposed AI Deployment Passport | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | All reject duplicate normative ownership, identify the missing two-level worked example, and preserve inheritance, authorization and release boundaries |
| F3: trusted PR/RI comparison | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | All reject candidate execution in the trusted boundary, require current-target merge evidence and retain unsupported parser-change outcomes |

These are ordinal 0/1/2 judgments against five predeclared criteria per task,
not percentages of repository understanding. There are three primary ties,
zero improvements reaching 2 and zero treatment losses. Each secondary
contrast also has three ties. The first assessor recorded 60 met criterion
judgments, 36 absent serious-error judgments and no required substantive
corrections; these are not 60 independent tasks or observed human interventions.

The model produced source-grounded answers about the tested concepts in every
condition, including ordinary-source access without either aid. The experiment
therefore shows that the added RI output was not necessary for these successful
answers under this budget. It does not reveal the model's internal mechanism
or prove that all subtler understanding was identical. Every answer reached
the top of the coarse scale: this ceiling limits sensitivity to smaller
differences and to improvements on harder work.

The assessor noted one optional clarity improvement in WF07: explicitly
condition the research-traceability companion on actual material findings.
It found the existing sentence consistent with the cited conditional process,
not an invented research-state change or a substantive criterion failure.
The original judgment is preserved without organizer rescoring.

## Measured burden and the frozen gates

Source/RI operations include source access, search/list calls, native queries,
their pagination, errors and rereads. They exclude delivery pages for the
starting message. The complete bytes of those starting pages remain counted.

| Primary task | AGENTS operations | AGENTS_RI operations | AGENTS input bytes | AGENTS_RI input bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| F1 | 34 | 31 | 256,324 | 372,109 |
| F2 | 52 | 53 | 388,609 | 557,455 |
| F3 | 33 | 24 | 209,532 | 213,503 |
| Total | 119 | 108 | 854,465 | 1,143,067 |

The burden is not uniformly lower: F2 uses one more source/RI operation, while
all three primary treatment answers receive more input bytes. F3 has the
largest operation reduction, but no measured conceptual-quality gain.

| Condition, all three tasks | Source/RI operations | Starting-message pages | All reader operations | Measured input UTF-8 bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NONE | 94 | 3 | 97 | 727,637 |
| AGENTS | 119 | 3 | 122 | 854,465 |
| RI | 72 | 30 | 102 | 890,405 |
| AGENTS_RI | 108 | 30 | 138 | 1,143,067 |

Measured input is the exact native bootstrap plus every rendered reader
response, including complete initial-message pages, wrappers, errors and
rereads. Initial material and archived copies are not charged twice. All
reader operations actually increase from 122 to 138 in the primary contrast
because full RI delivery takes more pages. Bytes are not model tokens, latency,
context reprocessing, billing or ROI; none of those were exposed reliably.

Preparation is separate overhead: one verification and three task-context CLI
outputs were produced and reused; pre-run smoke also invoked verification in
the two RI profiles. Each of six RI sessions received two prepared outputs.
WF06 additionally invoked `artifact-preflight` during its session; its output
and pagination are included in the session totals. The frozen task-context
stdout sizes were F1 117,817, F2 109,421 and F3 37,085 bytes, before starting
message and reader wrapping.

| Primary requirement | Observed | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Three usable pairs, no quality loss or new serious error | Met within the authorized instructional protocol | Necessary prerequisite met |
| Quality signal: at least two improvements reaching 2 | 0 | Not met |
| Efficiency signal: all six primary answers score 2 | 6 of 6 | Met |
| Efficiency signal: treatment operations at most 80% of control | 90.76% | Not met |
| Efficiency signal: treatment input bytes no greater than control | 133.78% | Not met |

Neither primary gate passes. The following secondary descriptions do not
rescue that decision:

| Added aid and comparison | Quality wins/losses/ties | Operation change | Input-byte change |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| RI over NONE | 0 / 0 / 3 | −23.4% | +22.4% |
| AGENTS over NONE | 0 / 0 / 3 | +26.6% | +17.4% |
| AGENTS over RI | 0 / 0 / 3 | +50.0% | +28.4% |

The RI-only comparison illustrates fewer retrieval operations with a larger
supplied payload. It is not demonstrated total cost savings. Likewise, these
read-only answer tasks do not test AGENTS' value for authorization, editing,
checkpoint discipline or safe operational behavior and do not justify removing it.

## Integrity, scoring independence and limits

The audit verified all 388 pinned source files, all 32 frozen input entries,
answer hashes, retained journals, exact rendered byte counts and permissions
for returned reads/search/list results. Every started source/RI response was
completely paged; required AGENTS and initial messages were fully read. All
sessions stayed within the 90-operation budget. There were no missing answers,
refusals, retries or detected reader exposure breaches.

WF10 made two denied requests, for the producer and benchmark README. They
returned access errors, not forbidden content; both errors and their bytes
are counted. Direct-read citation flags were reviewed: CHANGELOG is named as
a planned update; F3 parser/contract paths are interpretation members supported
by the read architecture/contract; WF10 also names explicitly unavailable
files. These are not claims of independent full reads or material incomplete
source reliance. No affected comparison is excluded on that basis.

Other tools remained technically available. Participants were instructed to
use only the reader, apart from saving their first answer. Logs attest that
reader's traffic, not absence of off-reader access, platform memory or hidden
context. No OS sandbox or independently verified platform-wide isolation is
claimed. This is the explicitly authorized September 21 restriction model,
not the stricter September 18 preparation prerequisite.

The separate fresh assessor received shuffled, opaque, verbatim answers,
unchanged criteria and pinned ordinary sources. It did not receive labels,
costs, logs, dispatch order or earlier studies. First scores were hashed and
remotely published at `c86409d9377b4737f7d980a12c2fe260527f1dc3` before the
condition join. WF10 and WF12 explicitly disclose absent aids in their access
statements, causing residual unblinding. Those statements were preserved;
the assessor disclosed them and excluded them from substantive scoring.
Full blinding is therefore not claimed. One agent assessor is not independent
human replication.

There are three organizer-authored convenience tasks and one realization per
cell. Selection was informed by repository material and earlier discussions;
it was not independent sampling, a randomized population study or a fully
counterbalanced repeated design. No significance, equivalence, population
effect, hidden-backend parity or full RI-EVAL-001 acceptance follows. Forced
full context, ample source access and the score ceiling limit transfer to
ordinary optional use, larger repositories and harder actual changes.

## Operational decision and evidence

Retain the existing optional RI route and cheap direct-owner fallback. These
results do not justify making full `context-for-task` delivery mandatory for
each task, nor removing RI. The concrete candidate considered was mandatory
loading, owned by the existing operational route in
`.github/REPOSITORY-INTELLIGENCE.md` and routed from root AGENTS. Delivery and
freshness are mechanically checkable; semantic benefit is not a CI property.
The candidate is deferred because neither frozen benefit gate passed; no
persistent guidance or automation change is applied.

The bounded study is complete; no expansion is started to seek a favorable
result. Normal repository work can continue under existing guidance. General
RI benefit remains uncertain and would require evidence from materially
different real work, not reinterpretation of these ties.
